findings.evidence: FASTO_RDF.owl contains rdfs:label literals explicitly typed as xsd:integer: L56273: <rdfs:label rdf:datatype="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#integer">318316003</rdfs:label> ; L58245: <rdfs:label rdf:datatype="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#integer">233915000</rdfs:label> ; L65222: <rdfs:label rdf:datatype="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#integer">acute hepatitis B with hepatitis D</rdfs:label> ; L81590: <rdfs:label rdf:datatype="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#integer">acute hepatic failure</rdfs:label> ; L93958: <rdfs:label rdf:datatype="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#integer">116084008</rdfs:label> ; L97053: <rdfs:label rdf:datatype="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#integer">pitavastatin</rdfs:label>
findings.explanation: Human-readable rdfs:label values are encoded with xsd:integer. Three of the lexical forms are not valid integers at all, and the numeric ones appear to be identifiers rather than labels. This can break datatype validation, label indexing, rendering, and search.
findings.suggested_fix: Use plain, language-tagged, or xsd:string labels for human-readable names. Move numeric identifiers into an identifier or cross-reference annotation property rather than rdfs:label.

findings.evidence: Same IRIs are declared both as owl:Class and owl:NamedIndividual. Examples: L108779: <owl:Class rdf:about="https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/FASTO/overweight">; L128798: <owl:NamedIndividual rdf:about="https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/FASTO/overweight">; L128799: <rdf:type rdf:resource="https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/FASTO/overweight"/>; L126145: <owl:Class rdf:about="https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/FTDM.owl#pramlintide">; L129269: <owl:NamedIndividual rdf:about="https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/FTDM.owl#pramlintide"/>.
findings.explanation: The same IRI is used as both an OWL class and an OWL named individual. Most affected IRIs also instantiate themselves. OWL 2 punning is syntactically possible, but this pattern creates a class-instance level ambiguity and can make downstream querying, reasoning, and maintenance error-prone.
findings.suggested_fix: Separate class IRIs from individual IRIs. Use a clear naming convention for instances, and remove self-instantiation unless intentional metamodeling is documented and required.
findings.additional_comment: 9 IRIs are both owl:Class and owl:NamedIndividual; 8 also have rdf:type assertions to themselves.

findings.evidence: Parsed primary RDF/XML contains 424 rdfs:label values assigned to more than one owl:Class, covering 903 class IRIs. Examples include: ; ; the duplicate label 'hypoglycemic coma' appears on three DDO.owl class IRIs; the duplicate label 'acute gonococcal urethritis' appears on five DDO.owl class IRIs.
findings.explanation: Multiple distinct class IRIs share the exact same rdfs:label without evidence that they are equivalent. Duplicate class labels create ambiguity for users, search, mapping, verbalization, and generated application code.
findings.suggested_fix: Review duplicate labels. Merge truly duplicate classes, assert explicit equivalence when appropriate, or disambiguate labels and synonyms so each distinct class can be identified reliably.
findings.additional_comment: 424 duplicate-label groups covering 903 class IRIs are listed in the entity field.

findings.evidence: Labels contain trailing spaces or embedded newlines. Examples: L24847: <rdfs:label>blood immunoglobulin a level increased AE </rdfs:label>; L36218-L36219: <rdfs:label xml:lang="en">blood folate level abnormal AE\n</rdfs:label>; L105619-L105620: <rdfs:label>gestational diabetes mellitus complicating pregnancy\n</rdfs:label>.
findings.explanation: Some labels contain trailing spaces or embedded newline characters. These invisible characters can produce duplicate-looking labels, failed exact matches, and inconsistent UI output.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalize label literals by trimming leading/trailing whitespace and replacing unintended embedded newlines with single spaces.
findings.additional_comment: 10 class labels with leading/trailing whitespace or newline characters were found.

findings.evidence: RDF/XML contains misspelled or inconsistent local names and labels, including: L6802: <owl:ObjectProperty rdf:about="http://www.w3.org/ns/ssn/hasMeasurmentProperty">; L8645: <rdf:Description rdf:about="http://www.w3.org/ns/ssn/measurmentCapability"/>; L10515: <owl:DatatypeProperty rdf:about="https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/FTDM/isPragnant">; L8989: <owl:DatatypeProperty rdf:about="https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/FASTO/hasPreferedBGUoM">; L10439: <owl:DatatypeProperty rdf:about="https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/FTDM/hasPreferedInsulinRegimen">; L7717: <owl:ObjectProperty rdf:about="https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/FTDM.owl#drugContradictDithDisease">; L123076: <rdfs:label xml:lang="en">BloodGlocoseReading</rdfs:label>.
findings.explanation: Several IRIs and labels contain spelling errors or inconsistent spellings such as 'measurment', 'glocose', 'pragnant', 'prefered', and 'Dith'. These errors can propagate into APIs, SPARQL queries, documentation, rules, and mappings.
findings.suggested_fix: Standardize spelling in labels and, where safe, deprecate misspelled IRIs in favor of correctly spelled replacement IRIs. Preserve backward-compatible mappings for existing users.
findings.additional_comment: 12 affected entities or labeled entities were found.

findings.flaw_category: Inconsistent ontology base and namespace strategy
findings.evidence: Ontology header and namespace declarations show inconsistent identity bases: L2: <rdf:RDF xmlns="http://www.semanticweb.org/shaker/ontologies/2018/9/untitled-ontology-475#"; L3: xml:base="http://www.semanticweb.org/shaker/ontologies/2018/9/untitled-ontology-475"; L35: <protege:defaultLanguage>en</protege:defaultLanguage>; L22: xmlns:FASTO="https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/FASTO/"; L23: xmlns:FTDM2="https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/FTDM/"; L13: xmlns:FTDM="https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/FTDM.owl#".
findings.explanation: The RDF/XML uses a semanticweb.org default base, while the ontology IRI is a BioPortal FASTO.owl IRI and entity namespaces mix FASTO slash IRIs, FTDM slash IRIs, and FTDM.owl hash IRIs. This makes identity management, versioning, imports, and term resolution harder to maintain.
findings.suggested_fix: Choose a canonical ontology IRI and canonical term namespace pattern. Align xml:base, default namespace, ontology IRI, version IRI, and entity IRIs consistently.

findings.flaw_category: Missing explicit imports for referenced external ontologies
findings.evidence: The parsed RDF graph contains 0 owl:imports triples for https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/FASTO.owl. The ontology annotation says it is based on BFO, SSN sensor ontology, and HL7 FHIR standard (L37: <dc:date rdf:datatype="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#date">2018-10-20</dc:date>), while the RDF/XML declares/uses external namespace entities such as L107026: <rdf:Description rdf:about="http://www.w3.org/ns/ssn/frequency"/> and L10748: <owl:Class rdf:about="http://hl7.org/fhir/address">.
findings.explanation: The ontology declares that it is based on external ontologies and uses or redeclares terms from external namespaces, but the authoritative RDF graph has no owl:imports statements. This weakens dependency management and can cause reasoners or applications to see only local copied fragments rather than the intended external ontologies.
findings.suggested_fix: Add explicit imports for required external ontologies or document that external terms are intentionally copied. Keep imported-vocabulary use separate from locally minted extensions.

findings.flaw_category: Domain terms minted in third-party namespaces
findings.evidence: Domain-specific entities are minted in external third-party namespaces. Examples: L127216: <owl:NamedIndividual rdf:about="http://swrl.stanford.edu/ontologies/built-ins/3.3/temporal.owl#lantus">; L127110: <!-- http://swrl.stanford.edu/ontologies/built-ins/3.3/temporal.owl#anxiety_AE -->; L106911: <owl:Class rdf:about="http://www.w3.org/ns/ssn/Abbott_FreeStyle_Lite">; L10882: <owl:Class rdf:about="http://hl7.org/fhir/alcoholIntakeObservation">.
findings.explanation: FASTO-specific drugs, adverse-event individuals, patient BAN instances, sensor products, and local FHIR-style observations are minted directly under namespaces controlled by other vocabularies. This creates ownership ambiguity and can collide with future or canonical terms from those vocabularies.
findings.suggested_fix: Mint local extension terms under the FASTO namespace and connect them to external ontology terms using subclassing, equivalence, mappings, or annotations where appropriate.
findings.additional_comment: The entity field lists representative affected entities directly observed in the RDF/XML.

findings.flaw_category: Concrete case data mixed into ontology
findings.evidence: The ontology includes concrete case-instance individuals and patient data. Examples: L128863: <owl:NamedIndividual rdf:about="https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/FASTO/patient_1">; L130602: <owl:NamedIndividual rdf:about="https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/FTDM/patient_1_profile">; L130066: <owl:NamedIndividual rdf:about="https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/FTDM/patient_1_carePlan_1">.
findings.explanation: The ontology contains concrete patient, practitioner, care-plan, profile, address, and sensor-output individuals. Mixing test or case data with the reusable ontology schema can reduce reusability, create privacy and governance risk, and complicate version control and reasoning.
findings.suggested_fix: Move case-specific ABox data into a separate example, test, or instance dataset. Keep the reusable ontology focused on schema-level classes, properties, constraints, and controlled individuals.
findings.additional_comment: 117 apparent case-specific individuals were identified by patient/practitioner/care-plan/profile/address/sensor naming patterns.

findings.flaw_category: Parallel class and individual IRIs with identical local names
findings.evidence: Several concepts have a class IRI and a separate individual IRI with the same local name. Examples: L123794: <owl:Class rdf:about="https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/FTDM.owl#aspart">; L129417: <owl:NamedIndividual rdf:about="https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/FTDM/aspart">; L106943: <owl:Class rdf:about="http://www.w3.org/ns/ssn/GlucoWise">; L131270: <owl:NamedIndividual rdf:about="https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/fhir.owl#GlucoWise">.
findings.explanation: Several classes and individuals are split into different IRIs while sharing the same local name. This is a weaker but still confusing form of class-instance name collision; it can make it difficult to determine whether a name refers to a class, an individual, or both.
findings.suggested_fix: Use distinct naming conventions for classes and instances, or document the intentional pattern. Where the separate IRIs represent the same referent incorrectly, merge or map them explicitly.
findings.additional_comment: 16 class/individual local-name collision pairs were found.

findings.evidence: Top/root property names are split by namespace and object/data property type. Examples: L7638: <owl:ObjectProperty rdf:about="https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/FTDM.owl#FASTOOntologyProperty"/>; L8536: <owl:DatatypeProperty rdf:about="http://www.w3.org/ns/ssn/FASTOOntologyProperty">; L3491: <owl:ObjectProperty rdf:about="http://hl7.org/fhir/FHIR_Property"/>; L8335: <owl:DatatypeProperty rdf:about="http://hl7.org/fhir/FHIRProperty"/>; L7025: <owl:ObjectProperty rdf:about="http://www.w3.org/ns/ssn/sensor_related_property"/>; L8694: <owl:DatatypeProperty rdf:about="http://www.w3.org/ns/ssn/sensorRelatedProperty"/>.
findings.explanation: The ontology uses nearly identical root property names in different namespaces and separates object-property and datatype-property roots by spelling variants. This makes property hierarchy navigation and maintenance harder and increases the risk of choosing the wrong superproperty.
findings.suggested_fix: Define a small, consistently named set of root object properties and root datatype properties in the local ontology namespace. Avoid spelling variants and avoid placing local root properties under external namespaces.

findings.evidence: Parsed RDF/XML shows 34 declared owl:ObjectProperty/owl:DatatypeProperty entities with neither rdfs:domain nor rdfs:range. Examples include: L3491: <owl:ObjectProperty rdf:about="http://hl7.org/fhir/FHIR_Property"/>; L8536: <owl:DatatypeProperty rdf:about="http://www.w3.org/ns/ssn/FASTOOntologyProperty">; L7638: <owl:ObjectProperty rdf:about="https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/FTDM.owl#FASTOOntologyProperty"/>; L8256: <owl:ObjectProperty rdf:about="https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/FTDM/hasFixedTwoshotsMorningShortActingInsulin">.
findings.explanation: Several declared properties have neither rdfs:domain nor rdfs:range. Domains and ranges are not mandatory in OWL, but for application ontologies their absence reduces validation power, discoverability, and maintainability.
findings.suggested_fix: For each property, add appropriate domain and range axioms or document why the property is intentionally unconstrained.
findings.additional_comment: 34 properties with neither domain nor range are listed.

findings.evidence: The object property is declared both symmetric and transitive: L7727: <owl:ObjectProperty rdf:about="https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/FTDM.owl#drugContradictWithDrug">; L7729: <rdf:type rdf:resource="http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#SymmetricProperty"/>; L7730: <rdf:type rdf:resource="http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#TransitiveProperty"/>.
findings.explanation: The contraindication-like property drugContradictWithDrug is declared both symmetric and transitive. Symmetry may be plausible for pairwise contradiction, but transitivity can propagate contradictions through chains and produce broad inferred relationships that may not be intended.
findings.suggested_fix: Review whether transitivity is semantically intended for drug contradiction. If contradictions are pairwise, keep symmetry if appropriate and remove transitivity or replace it with explicit rule logic that matches the intended inference.
findings.additional_comment: This is reported as a modeling risk because the RDF/XML directly shows the property characteristics, but intended clinical semantics are not supplied.

findings.evidence: Some local names encode CURIE-like identifiers or slashes inside a fragment, which makes namespace identity and QName tooling fragile. Examples: L126741: <owl:Class rdf:about="https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/FTDM.owl#PATO:0001995">; L8088: <owl:ObjectProperty rdf:about="https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/FTDM.owl#TIME:0000004">; L106902: <owl:Class rdf:about="http://www.w3.org/2006/time#TIME:0000002">; L126761: <owl:Class rdf:about="https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/FTDM.owl#ReliOn/HumuLIN_R">.
findings.explanation: Some entity IRIs contain CURIE-like local names after a hash, such as PATO:0001995, or slash characters inside a fragment. These IRIs are legal as IRIs but are fragile for QName-based tools, namespace governance, and human interpretation.
findings.suggested_fix: Use canonical external IRIs for external identifiers where possible, or encode local names with a consistent safe separator. Avoid CURIE strings and path separators inside hash fragments.

findings.evidence: Ontology metadata contains an empty rdfs:comment: L40: <owl:versionInfo>1.0</owl:versionInfo>
findings.explanation: The ontology has an empty English rdfs:comment. Empty annotations add noise and may be rendered as blank documentation fields.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the empty comment or replace it with useful ontology-level documentation.

findings.flaw_category: Missing human-readable labels on custom entities
findings.evidence: Parsed primary RDF/XML shows 1695 custom FASTO/FTDM/FHIR/SSN/unit entities without any rdfs:label assertion. Examples include declarations with no label in their blocks: L1434: <owl:ObjectProperty rdf:about="http://hl7.org/fhir/Address.city">; L108291: <owl:Class rdf:about="https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/FASTO/breakfastGlucoseObservationValue">; L130066: <owl:NamedIndividual rdf:about="https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/FTDM/patient_1_carePlan_1">; L106911: <owl:Class rdf:about="http://www.w3.org/ns/ssn/Abbott_FreeStyle_Lite">.
findings.explanation: A large number of custom or locally maintained entities have no rdfs:label. Missing labels reduce readability, verbalization quality, browsing, search, and ontology reuse.
findings.suggested_fix: Add stable, human-readable rdfs:label annotations to custom classes, properties, and individuals, using a consistent language-tagging policy.
findings.additional_comment: 1695 custom FASTO/FTDM/FHIR/SSN/unit entities without rdfs:label are listed.
